For q-130256, yy' makes I nonlinear, while II and III are linear combinations of derivatives with coefficients depending only on x. Linearity gives 10 for q-64900 and x²−1 for q-79606. For q-181958, option 2 contains exactly (p,w), (q,w), (p,z), and (q,z), matching the completed source diagram despite different cropping. Cartesian-product cardinalities are 10·10=100 and 7·6=42. The homogeneous equations give Ae^(−6x) and Ae^(5x). Substituting y_p=x²/2−x gives 2y_p'+2y_p=x²−2. The probability answers follow respectively from the indicated cell, summing three disjoint cells, summing four cells in the union without double counting, and summing the X=2 row. To see why, we first evaluate the left-hand side of the linearity condition:\n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}{D}_{1}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) & =\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})+(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})\\frac{\\text{d}}{\\text{d}x}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) \\\\  & =a\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+b\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}^{2}{y}_{1}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}x}+{b}^{2}{y}_{2}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}x}+ab({y}_{1}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}x}+{y}_{2}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}x})\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\nThis is not the same as the right-hand side, because\n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}a{D}_{1}({y}_{1})+b{D}_{1}({y}_{2}) & =a[\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{y}_{1}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}x}]+b[\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{y}_{2}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}x}] \\\\  & =a\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+b\\frac{{\\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}{x}^{2}}+a{y}_{1}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\\text{d}x}+b{y}_{2}\\frac{\\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\\text{d}x}.\\,\\times \\end{aligned}\n$$\n\n- The second operator is indeed linear.
